description: On a runner with Docker and systemd. Exited containers: one OOM-killed (16 MiB limit, a shell that allocates) always alerts, worded as an out-of-memory kill; docker stop giving 143 (sleep behind --init) and 137 (a shell as PID 1 that ignores TERM) is named in the status under usrStoppedExitAction Warn and alerts under Alert; exit code 1 alerts as before; usrIncludeLogs Yes puts the last log lines in the diagnostic and says so in the status. Baseline age: saved state an hour old gives the restart-loop alert; made 7 hours old, the run takes a new baseline, raises no restart alert, resets breach streaks and says so. The state directory /var/lib/tc-docker-monitor: a pre-made symlink there is not followed and one not owned by root is not used (the check runs without saved state and says why); a symlink at the state file is replaced, its target untouched. usrExclude starting with - is a pattern. A docker shim that never answers (also one that ignores TERM, and one that hangs only docker stats) gives 'Docker did not answer within 60 seconds', exit 1, inside 90 seconds, nothing left running and a sibling in the caller's process group untouched. docker.service stopped with docker.socket listening: exit 0, no docker command run, Docker still stopped. No docker command but a socket: exit 1; a client only in /snap/bin is found through the appended PATH. GNU bash 4.2 runs the main paths without an unbound-variable crash. The first step reads the script itself: its time-limit functions sit in one block marked tc-docker bounded (a block CI compares with the other Docker monitors' copies), and its tc-docker running block says it is identical in every tc-docker component.

steps.label: Shared blocks: bounded, systemd_up and docker_unit_loaded are defined once each, inside one block marked tc-docker bounded, and the tc-docker running block's first line says it is identical in every tc-docker component
steps.run: f=Monitors/docker-container-health-and-resource-usage-lin/docker-container-health-and-resource-usage-lin.sh; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "cannot find $f from $(pwd)"; exit 1; }; echo "bounded block: $(grep -c '^# >>> tc-docker bounded: ' $f) start, $(grep -c '^# <<< tc-docker bounded$' $f) end"; echo "functions inside it: $(sed -n '/^# >>> tc-docker bounded: /,/^# <<< tc-docker bounded$/p' $f | grep -cE '^(bounded|systemd_up|docker_unit_loaded)\(\) \{')"; echo "the same functions in the whole script: $(grep -cE '^(bounded|systemd_up|docker_unit_loaded)\(\) \{' $f)"; echo "running block first line: $(grep -c '^# >>> tc-docker running: identical in every tc-docker component; change them together\.$' $f)"
outputContains: the same functions in the whole script: 3

steps.label: Test helpers: tc-test-run (runs the monitor the way the harness does, timed, under /bin/bash or bash 4.2), tc-test-left, tc-test-dstate, tc-test-state, tc-test-clean; a tiny local image tc-test-base:1; one running container tc-run1
steps.run:
set -e
M="$PWD/Monitors/docker-container-health-and-resource-usage-lin/docker-container-health-and-resource-usage-lin.sh"
test -f "$M"
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-run <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-run [--bash42] [VAR=value...]: run the monitor as the harness does (a clean
# environment and the agent's root PATH); print its output, exit code and seconds taken.
b=/bin/bash; if [ "${1:-}" = --bash42 ]; then b=/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash; shift; fi
t0=$(date +%s)
env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root "$@" "$b" "@MONITOR@"
rc=$?
secs=$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))
echo "exit $rc after $secs seconds, under $("$b" -c 'echo "bash $BASH_VERSION"')"
[ "$secs" -lt 90 ] && echo "result inside 90 seconds"
exit 0
EOF
sed -i "s|@MONITOR@|$M|" /usr/local/bin/tc-test-run
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-left <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-left: any docker shim process still running, from ps.
sleep 1
echo "--- ps -eo pid,ppid,pgid,etime,args, docker shims and their children:"
ps -eo pid,ppid,pgid,etime,args | grep -E '[/]usr/local/sbin/docker|[s]leep 600|[t]c-test-shim' || echo "no docker client or shim process left"
EOF
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-dstate <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-dstate LABEL: what systemd says about Docker.
echo "$1: systemctl is-active docker.service docker.socket -> $(systemctl is-active docker.service docker.socket | paste -sd' ')"
EOF
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-state <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-state: the state directory and the state file, or that they are not there.
d=/var/lib/tc-docker-monitor; f=$d/monitor-state.tsv
ls -lad "$d" 2>&1
if [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ]; then echo "--- $f (now $(date +%s)):"; ls -la "$f"; cat "$f"; else echo "(no state file)"; fi
EOF
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-clean <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-clean: remove every container except tc-run1, and the monitor's state.
for c in $(docker ps -aq --no-trunc); do
    [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.Name}}' "$c")" = /tc-run1 ] || docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null
done
rm -rf /var/lib/tc-docker-monitor
docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' | sort
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/tc-test-run /usr/local/bin/tc-test-left /usr/local/bin/tc-test-dstate /usr/local/bin/tc-test-state /usr/local/bin/tc-test-clean
# A tiny image built here (sh, sleep, true and their libraries), so no registry is needed.
r=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$r/bin"
for b in /bin/sh /bin/sleep /bin/true; do
    cp "$(readlink -f "$b")" "$r/bin/$(basename "$b")"
    for l in $(ldd "$b" | grep -oE '/[^ ]+'); do mkdir -p "$r$(dirname "$l")"; cp -L "$l" "$r$l" 2>/dev/null || true; done
done
tar -C "$r" -c . | docker import - tc-test-base:1 >/dev/null; rm -rf "$r"
docker run --rm tc-test-base:1 /bin/sh -c 'echo "tc-test-base:1 runs"'
for c in $(docker ps -aq); do docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null; done
rm -rf /var/lib/tc-docker-monitor
docker run -d --name tc-run1 tc-test-base:1 /bin/sleep 86400 >/dev/null
echo "helpers installed for $M"

steps.label: bash 4.2: build GNU bash 4.2 from the GNU release (sha256 checked) into /opt/tc-bash42; it has the bug: an empty array is unbound under set -u
steps.run:
set -e
d=$(mktemp -d); cd "$d"
for u in https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/bash/bash-4.2.tar.gz https://ftpmirror.gnu.org/bash/bash-4.2.tar.gz; do
  curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o bash-4.2.tar.gz "$u" && break
done
echo 'a27a1179ec9c0830c65c6aa5d7dab60f7ce1a2a608618570f96bfa72e95ab3d8  bash-4.2.tar.gz' | sha256sum -c -
tar xzf bash-4.2.tar.gz
cd bash-4.2
# 2011 C: -std=gnu89 goes in CC so it also reaches the build-time tools (CC_FOR_BUILD), which a
# newer gcc defaulting to C23 otherwise refuses; the old-style warnings stay warnings.
W='-O1 -fpermissive -Wno-implicit-function-declaration -Wno-implicit-int -Wno-int-conversion -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types -Wno-return-mismatch'
gcc --version | head -n 1
CC='gcc -std=gnu89' CFLAGS="$W" CFLAGS_FOR_BUILD="$W" ./configure --without-bash-malloc --disable-nls >configure.log 2>&1 || { tail -n 30 configure.log; exit 1; }
make -j"$(nproc)" >make.log 2>&1 || { grep -m 20 'error:' make.log; tail -n 30 make.log; exit 1; }
install -D -m 755 bash /opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash
/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash -c 'echo "built bash $BASH_VERSION"'
/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash -c 'set -u; a=(); echo "${a[@]}"' 2>&1 || true

steps.label: OOM: tc-oom, memory limit 16 MiB and no swap, runs a shell that doubles a string until the kernel kills it; Docker can record OOMKilled a moment after the exit, so this waits up to 30 seconds for it
steps.run: docker run --name tc-oom -m 16m --memory-swap 16m tc-test-base:1 /bin/sh -c 'a=xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx; while :; do a="$a$a"; done'; for i in $(seq 30); do [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.OOMKilled}}' tc-oom)" = true ] && break; sleep 1; done; docker inspect -f 'tc-oom: exit {{.State.ExitCode}} OOMKilled {{.State.OOMKilled}}' tc-oom

steps.label: OOM-killed: always an alert, worded as such (usrStoppedExitAction Warn, the default)
outputContains: STATUS=Docker: tc-oom: killed for running out of memory (OOM)

steps.label: OOM-killed, usrStoppedExitAction Alert: the same alert
outputContains: STATUS=Docker: tc-oom: killed for running out of memory (OOM)

steps.label: docker stop: tc-stop143 (sleep behind docker's init, which passes TERM on, so it exits 143) and tc-stop137 (a shell as PID 1 ignores TERM, so docker stop KILLs it: 137)
steps.run: set -e; docker run -d --init --name tc-stop143 tc-test-base:1 /bin/sleep 600 >/dev/null; docker run -d --name tc-stop137 tc-test-base:1 /bin/sh -c 'sleep 600' >/dev/null; sleep 1; docker stop -t 2 tc-stop143 tc-stop137 >/dev/null; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}}: exit {{.State.ExitCode}} OOMKilled {{.State.OOMKilled}}' tc-stop143 tc-stop137

steps.label: Baseline age: tc-loop restarts every second (restart: always); wait for 3 restarts; first run records a baseline
steps.run: docker run -d --name tc-loop --restart always tc-test-base:1 /bin/sh -c 'sleep 1; exit 3' >/dev/null; for i in $(seq 60); do n=$(docker inspect -f '{{.RestartCount}}' tc-loop); [ "$n" -ge 3 ] && break; sleep 1; done; echo "tc-loop restarts: $n"; [ "$n" -ge 3 ] && echo 'at least 3 restarts'

steps.run: set -e; real=$(command -v docker); test "$real" != /usr/local/sbin/docker; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' '# tc-test-shim: records every docker command' 'echo "$*" >> /var/tmp/tc-docker-calls' "exec $real \"\$@\"" > /usr/local/sbin/docker; chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/docker; hash -r; : > /var/tmp/tc-docker-calls; tc-test-dstate before; systemctl stop docker.service 2>/dev/null; tc-test-dstate stopped; echo "docker commands run: $(wc -l < /var/tmp/tc-docker-calls)"
